report.reportTitle: Critical Malware Threat Analysis — Emotet + PowerShell Dropper

executiveSummary.summary: AegisX has identified a critical-severity Emotet-variant malware campaign targeting the Finance department of your organization. A macro-enabled Word document was delivered via spearphishing email and successfully convinced a user to enable macro execution. The attack chain includes PowerShell-based payload download, credential harvesting via LSASS access, and exfiltration attempt over Tor-routed HTTPS. The threat was blocked at the exfiltration stage by the AegisX endpoint agent.
executiveSummary.businessImpact: HIGH — Active threat with credential exposure. Finance department user credentials potentially compromised. Risk of lateral movement to adjacent systems. Potential PII and financial data exposure.
executiveSummary.primaryRisk: Credential theft leading to unauthorized account access and potential ransomware deployment as secondary payload.
executiveSummary.recommendedPriority: P1 — Immediate Response Required. Escalate to CISO and initiate IR procedure IR-005.

recommendedActions.details: Immediately disconnect WS-FIN-042 from corporate network. Enable host firewall to block all traffic except SOC investigation channels.
Disable sarah.johnson@company.com in Active Directory. Revoke all active sessions and OAuth tokens in Azure AD.
Force password reset for the affected user and all users in the Finance OU. Issue new smart card certificates.
Block payload-delivery-cdn.net and update-microsoft-cdn.com at DNS gateway, proxy, and firewall. Apply to all egress points.
Add 185.220.101.47 and 91.108.56.178 to threat blocklist on perimeter firewall and SIEM correlation rules.

recommendedActions.action: Remove malicious attachment from email system
recommendedActions.details: Purge all instances of Invoice_Q4_2024_Payroll.docm from Exchange Online. Search for similar attachments from the same sender domain.
Deploy AegisX threat hunt query for Emotet campaign IOCs across all endpoints. Focus on Finance and Executive department devices.

containmentSteps: Step 1: Activate Incident Response Plan IR-005 — Malware Containment
Step 2: Isolate affected endpoint WS-FIN-042 via NAC policy enforcement
Step 3: Capture live memory image using Volatility before system shutdown
Step 4: Acquire forensic disk image for offline analysis
Step 5: Block all identified IOCs at network perimeter
Step 6: Disable compromised user account and revoke all tokens
Step 7: Notify CISO, Legal, and Compliance teams per IR protocol
Step 8: Search email gateway for related phishing campaign artifacts
Step 9: Apply emergency YARA signatures to EDR for real-time detection
recoverySteps: Step 1: Conduct full forensic analysis of affected endpoint before reimaging
Step 2: Reimage affected endpoint with clean gold image from trusted source
Step 3: Restore user data from last verified clean backup (pre-incident)
Step 4: Re-enable user account after confirming credential reset completion
Step 5: Apply additional monitoring rules for Finance department endpoints for 30 days
Step 6: Mandatory security awareness training for all Finance department staff
Step 7: Review and update email filtering rules for macro-enabled documents
Step 8: Conduct post-incident review within 72 hours and update IR playbook
Step 9: File regulatory notification if PII exposure is confirmed (GDPR Article 33)
